app.title: GeoDFN – Geologically Consistent Discrete Fracture Network Generator
app.summary: A person picks a ready-made scenario or starts blank, then sets the run: how many realizations, a run name, an output folder, the size of the 2D domain and how many fracture sets there are. They choose an aperture model and fill in its parameters. For each set they enter an intensity and a buffer zone, and choose a distribution for length, spatial placement and orientation, each with its own parameters. Generating places the fractures for every realization while a progress bar runs and reports how many converged. They then step through the realizations as tabs, each with a map of the fractures coloured by set, an orientation rose diagram and summary statistics, and download every output file as a ZIP.

task.text: Generate an ensemble of statistically consistent stochastic 2D fracture networks from per-set distribution parameters, check each realization, and export the files a flow simulator needs.

data.text: Parameters for each fracture set (intensity, buffer zone, and the distributions for length, spatial placement and orientation, plus an aperture model) go in. What comes out is a set of generated realizations: line segments with coordinates, lengths and apertures inside a rectangular domain.
data.item: one generated realization of the fracture network: a set of fracture segments, each tagged with its set

stage.text: building stochastic fracture models from statistics measured on outcrops, before running flow and transport simulations

mechanism.text: A form sets the domain and the aperture model, and a tab for each fracture set holds three side-by-side columns of distribution choices. Each column shows only the parameter fields its chosen distribution needs. A generate button runs the stochastic placement with a progress bar, and the results appear as one tab per realization, each pairing a fracture map with an orientation rose diagram and summary metrics, plus one ZIP download for all the outputs.

field.text: stochastic discrete fracture network modelling from outcrop statistics in structural geology

workflow.name: generate an ensemble of stochastic realizations from parameter distributions

steps.step: start from a preset or a blank configuration
steps.here: A Preset dropdown loads a whole scenario (a field-calibrated case, a single set, orthogonal sets, conjugate sets) into every field, or 'Custom' leaves everything blank.

steps.step: set the size of the run and the domain
steps.here: Number of realizations (1–1000), run name, output folder, domain length X and width Y in metres, and number of fracture sets (1–5).

steps.step: choose a model and fill in its parameters
steps.here: The aperture method (subLinear, constant, Barton-Bandis, Lepillier) shows only its own inputs, such as scaling coefficient and exponent, JRC and JCS, or the in-situ stresses, E and ν.

steps.step: describe each group by its distributions
steps.here: In each 'Set N' tab, enter intensity (m⁻¹) and a buffer zone (constant or linear in length), then pick the length, spatial and orientation distributions (log-normal, power-law, exponential, von Mises, uniform, constant) and fill in their parameters.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: 'Generate DFN' places the fractures for every realization, updates a progress bar per realization, and warns how many failed to converge before hitting the placement retry limit.

One tab per realization shows the fracture map coloured by set, a rose diagram of orientations in 10° bins, and metrics: total fractures, total intensity, mean and max length, mean aperture, and the fracture count per set.
'Download Results (ZIP)' bundles the run's output folder: coordinates, apertures, input and output property files, and pictures.

distinctive: Each set has its own length, spatial placement and orientation distributions, and each shows only the parameter fields that distribution needs.
A buffer zone around each fracture, either constant or scaled with its length, constrains placement, and realizations that cannot fit everything are dropped and counted.
Apertures come from a choice of physical models, including stress-dependent ones that take in-situ stresses and strike.
Every realization gets its own orientation rose diagram and an achieved intensity that can be checked against the target intensity entered for each set.
The output is an ensemble of equiprobable realizations, not a single answer, and is written as files for flow and transport simulators.
